name: Hypnotic Pattern

operational.targets: Choose a point you perceive with line of effect: within 60 feet for actual Enchantment casting access, or within 30 feet for actual Illusion casting access. Center a fixed 30-foot cube on that point, extending 15 feet along each axis. At resolution snapshot every creature physically in the cube with line of effect from its center that can actually see the pattern, including allies and yourself; no selective omission. The numeric range field records the maximum mode, not permission for Illusion to use 60 feet.
operational.duration: Concentration, up to one minute, with independent damage/rousing endings per affected creature. In initiative, the maximum ends at the caster's tenth future regular-turn START after application, excluding any start already underway/passed. If begun outside initiative, the maximum is 60 elapsed seconds. Preserve the original virtual marker/absolute deadline through initiative changes, extra turns, absence and planar travel; no timing-mode change resets it.
operational.resolution: Use the actual class’s school and rank-3/5-RP access. Enchantment access belongs to Bard, Crimson Agent, Mirrorsage, Thief, Wizard and Paladin at their preserved levels; Monk’s actual mode is Illusion. Each eligible creature makes a Wisdom save. Success: no new components. Failure independently attempts Core Charmed toward you and actual Incapacitated. Charmed immunity blocks only Charmed; the Incapacitated component has its own defenses and shared hard-control allowance. A blocked hard component can leave independently legal Charmed. Apply the NEW spell-specific atomic initial batch in the shared rank-three manuscript: snapshot eligibility, resolve saves and legal components, apply every target’s components/immediate consequences, then process queued teardown of this Pattern if your own Incapacitated ended its concentration. Do not abort later targets because of iteration order.
operational.effect: Actual Charmed and Incapacitated retain their separate printed effects. Incapacitated ends applicable existing concentration and denies its ordinary covered action types; it does not inherently set Speed to 0. If self-Incapacitated ends your Pattern, other targets still receive that same initial batch and its real immediate consequences before this cast’s maintained components are removed. The visible lights remain in the fixed cube while concentration lasts but grant no general illumination, concealment or sight through obscurity. This is an initial snapshot: later entrants or initially ineligible creatures do not receive new applications. Later loss of sight does not end an existing application. End both still-present components from this cast on a creature when it receives positive post-defense/pre-temp-HP damage, or when another creature within physical reach uses an Action to rouse one selected Pattern application. Damage resolution preserves already-established hit/critical outcomes. No repeat saves.
operational.scaling: None. No automatic increase in range, targets, duration, magnitude or uses.
operational.limitations: A fully prevented zero damage packet does not wake; a positive packet can wake even when temporary HP or an HP floor prevents ordinary HP loss. Rousing ends one actual cast’s application only, not every Pattern or unrelated condition source. If the helper cannot distinguish several Pattern applications, select one by stable application order without disclosing hidden source metadata. Recasts create independent sources subject to actual concentration transitions and each new hard-component check; an exact multiple-concentration feature does not convert them into refreshes. A Charmed-only remnant receives no invented repeat save. No unaware, Unconscious, Prone, Speed 0 or forced item drop is added. Ordinary darkness/obscurity can prevent initial actual sight even though the pattern itself is visible. Hard whole-Action/turn components share the combined source-character/target/encounter allowance across class features, spells and companions. Successful establishment claims it once, not per affected turn. Ending, replacing, dispelling or suppressing a hard component never refunds the history. A blocked hard component gains no invented fallback; independently printed components retain their actual defenses. Initial prevention leaves no deferred hard application. Later suppression of an established component preserves its clock and spent history. Actual boss/control immunities remain effective. The accompanying ENCHANTMENT_RANK3_INTEGRATION_PLAYTEST.md supplies the expressly bound timing/component procedure; it grants no extra turn, action, hidden information or source access. Actual class access/repertoire, legal action/components/RP, concentration transitions, Dissonance/Refrain and paid cast/counter order follow SPELL_INTEGRATION_RULES.md. A legal cast pays before hidden eligibility/effect resolution; failure or countering refunds nothing and restores no displaced concentration. V is audible, S needs the ordinary usable hand, and F is the normal class focus. Saves use the actual casting class's spell DC and binary-save rules. Hidden eligibility supplies no free diagnostic. Creature type alone supplies no mental immunity; Charmed-only immunity has only its actual condition scope. No generic upcast, extra action budget or resource generation.
operational.designNotes: PRESERVED: both schools/rank-3/5-RP class access, Action/V/S/F, Enchantment range 60 and Illusion range 30, concentration minute, Charmed/Incapacitated; Illusion supplies 30-foot cube and WIS. NEW: harmonized cube/save for Enchantment, perceived center/center-LoE/sight snapshot, separate components, waking, and spell-specific atomic self-concentration cleanup. As one existing Bonus Action, consciously move any/all surviving lights once, each along a continuous non-solid path no longer than 30 feet. Each new destination must be perceived with line of effect from the caster and within 60 feet. The path may curve around obstacles but never pass through solid matter, teleport or exceed its actual distance budget. The 60-foot caster-to-light tether is checked continuously during movement of caster or light: exceeding it ends that light immediately, even if a proposed path would later return. One light ending leaves the rest. Losing caster-to-light line of effect after creation does not itself end an unmoving light; it still illuminates subject to ordinary physical barriers. A later command still needs its destination’s perception/line of effect. Lights otherwise stay at their points; no automatic following, formation lock or autonomous movement.
operational.scaling: None. No automatic increase in damage, range, target count, duration, uses or magnitude.

Ordinary lighting can remove mundane darkness as the actual reason something was unseen; other concealment/senses remain. Commands grant no extra Bonus Action. Actual multiple-concentration features do not bypass the one-set-per-caster cap.
